correctness.rationale: Cyclic gap lengths d_i≥r+1 for an m-set give nonnegative slack g_i with Σg_i=s. Counting marked selected vertices and weak compositions yields m|V|=L C(m+s−1,s). For a fixed common (m−1)-subset, at most one gap allows reinsertion, because two gaps of length ≥2(r+1) contradict total length L<(m+1)(r+1); feasible positions are an interval of length ≤s+1≤3. Thus every exchange moves at distance ≤2≤r. Unit slides transfer one slack unit to an adjacent gap. With s=1 all degrees 2 and slack circulates, giving connected C_L; with s=2, one double unit gap or two single-unit gaps gives exactly four distinct moves per configuration. Slack transportation collects and rotates surplus, giving connectedness. Three pairwise exchange-adjacent maximum sets must share m−1 vertices by maximality, hence one feasible 3-point interval and one displacement-two edge; exactly L double-gap configurations supply 2L incidences/2=L such edges and L triangles. Independent brute-force adjacency/independent-set/exchange enumeration checked 27 complete small (r,m,s) configurations including components, degrees and triangles; infinite proof is the gap argument.
residual_risks: Independent computations are bounded and do not replace the analytical all-parameter proof.

value.rationale: Near-packed maximum independent sets of natural cycle powers exhibit a sharp frozen→cyclic→4-regular connected reconfiguration transition when exactly two excess sites become available. Exact triangle count measures local move redundancy and distinguishes the two-slack regime; extends directly to antiprism graphs. Motivated structural classification, not mere recounting of an independence polynomial.
residual_risks: Applicability is limited to the theorem hypotheses, not a generalization to all related objects or interventions.

final_claim: For r,m≥2, L=(r+1)m+s, s∈{0,1,2}, maximum independent sets of C_L^r have size m. Their one-vertex-exchange graph is (r+1) isolated points for s=0; the cycle C_L for s=1; and a connected 4-regular graph with L(m+1)/2 vertices, L(m+1) edges and exactly L triangles for s=2. For these maximum sets all token-jumps are slides of distance at most 2.
limitations: An older exhaustive graph-reconfiguration classification might contain this special cycle-power computation without using slack terminology.
No classification for s≥3 or exact diameter of the connected s=2 graph; exclusions of m=1 or r=1 are essential.
Finite direct enumeration independently checks a bounded grid, not all r,m.
No external expert attestation or Lean formal proof; computations corroborate but do not establish the infinite theorem.
